_what: Limits and words for a screen made of shared parts (src/screen-spec.mjs). An AI sends the screen as lines, each one change (or a list of changes) in RFC 6902 form to { root, elements, state, reads }; every complete line is applied and drawn at once (src/workspace/parts-screen.tsx). A line that is not a change, or that changes something a line may not touch, is left out and said; it never stops the lines after it. Limits bound what one screen may hold and how much one line or one stream may be. A tool whose screen is a parts screen and that has no invoke is a screen by itself (src/workshop.mjs): it is saved with `screen_only_licence` when it names none, and needs no placement or sample.

words.part_failed: This part could not be shown.
words.unknown_part: {key}: "{type}" is not a part screens can use. Parts: {parts}.
words.not_element: {key}: an element is an object with a type and props.
words.dropped_prop: {key}: {type} has no prop {prop}; it was left out.
words.moved_field: {key}: "{field}" belongs on the element, not in props; it was moved.
words.unknown_action: {key}: the {event} action "{action}" is not a declared request or setState; it was left out.
words.no_children: {key}: {type} holds no other elements; its children were left out.
words.dangling_child: {key}: child "{child}" was never sent; it was left out.
words.no_root: The screen names no root element. Send {"op":"add","path":"/root","value":"<element key>"} first.
words.bad_path: Line {line} changes {path}; a line may change only /root, /elements, /state and /reads.
words.bad_op: Line {line}: {op} is not a change a screen takes; use add, replace or remove.
words.too_long_line: Line {line} is longer than {most} characters and was left out.
words.too_many_lines: The screen is more than {most} lines; the rest were left out.
words.too_many_elements: The screen holds more than {most} elements; the rest were left out.
words.bad_read: reads {path}: names "{request}", which is not a declared GET request; it was left out.
words.cycle: {key} holds itself; that part was not drawn again.

ai.guide: To make a new screen from shared parts instead of naming one, send parts: the screen as lines, one JSON change per line (RFC 6902 add, replace or remove on {root, elements, state, reads}), root first, so the person sees it grow as you write: {"op":"add","path":"/root","value":"main"} then {"op":"add","path":"/elements/main","value":{"type":"Card","props":{},"children":["title"]}} then each child. An element is {type, props, children, on, visible, repeat}; children are keys of other elements. A prop may be {"$state":"/path"}, {"$bindState":"/path"} (read and written back), {"$template":"Hi ${/name}"}, {"$cond":{"$state":"/x","eq":1},"$then":..,"$else":..}; inside repeat ({"statePath":"/rows","key":"id"}) {"$item":"field"}, {"$bindItem":"field"} and {"$index":true}. on maps an event to {action, params, result}: action is setState (params {path, value}) or the name of one of requests, the screen's named requests with the same declarations as save_tool's screen.requests (fixed /work/api/ paths and methods, or resource_operation); params may use {"$event":true}. reads fills state from GET requests: {"/rows":{"request":"<GET request>","pick":"/rows"}}. label names the screen; it is kept as one of the person's tools (screen picks one to change; delete_tool removes it). Parts and their props: {parts}.
ai.needs_label: A new screen needs a label (its name), or screen naming the tool id of one of your parts screens to change.
